verses.1: For the Chief Musician. With stringed instruments. A maskil of David.
verses.2: When the Ziphites came and said to Saul, “Is David not hiding among us?”
verses.3: God, in your name save me, and by your might judge me.
verses.4: God, hear my prayer, give ear to the words of my mouth.
verses.5: For strangers have risen against me, and violent men have sought my life. They do not set God before them. Selah.
verses.6: Indeed, God is my helper. The Lord is the one who sustains my life.
verses.7: Return evil to my adversaries. In your truth, destroy them.
verses.8: I will willingly sacrifice to you. I will praise your name, O Lord, for it is good.
verses.9: For you have rescued me from every trouble. And my eyes have seen my enemies.

notes:
Notes
- v. 2: The Hebrew text indicates that the Ziphites informed Saul about David's hiding place. The translation follows the Hebrew directly.
- v. 5: The word "Selah" is retained as in the original, though its precise meaning remains uncertain.
- v. 8: "I will willingly sacrifice" reflects the Hebrew נְדָבָה, which means "willingly" or "freely."
